`releaseTask` (`src/domain/lifecycle.ts`) only guarded against re-releasing a `done` task, not a `cancelled` one. `cancelTask` clears `owner_session_id`/`lock_expires_at` to `NULL` when it cancels a task, so a `release_task` call that arrives after cancellation (e.g. a worker session releasing on shutdown/retry without knowing the task was cancelled in the meantime) sailed past the conflict check — since the owner is already `null` there's nothing to conflict with — and unconditionally reset the row to `status = 'pending'`, `owner_session_id = NULL`, `lock_expires_at = NULL`. That silently resurrected the task for `get_next_task` while leaving `cancellation_reason` in place, exactly matching the reported symptom, with no error and nothing logged since the call itself "succeeded".

## Fix

Extended the terminal-state guard in `releaseTask` to also reject `cancelled` tasks, mirroring the existing `done` check (`Task <id> is already cancelled, nothing to release`). This only blocks the resurrection path — it doesn't touch the conflict-check/force logic used for normal in-progress releases, and `claimTask`/`cancelTask` are untouched (they already rejected cancelled tasks correctly).

Added a regression test in `tests/lifecycle.test.ts` asserting that releasing a cancelled task throws, leaves `status`/`cancellation_reason` unchanged, and that `get_next_task` still returns nothing for it.

Note: I don't have a shell/execution tool in this session, so I wasn't able to run the test suite — worth running `npm test` (or your usual command) to confirm before merging.

## Root cause

`releaseTask` (`src/domain/lifecycle.ts`) only rejected calls on a `done` task, not a `cancelled` one. `cancelTask` clears `owner_session_id`/`lock_expires_at` to `NULL` on cancellation (so the cancelled task looks unowned), but leaves `cancellation_reason` set. If whoever held the task before cancellation later calls `release_task` on it, the ownership check trivially passes (no active lock), and `releaseTask` unconditionally flips it back to `status = 'pending'` — resurrecting it with no error, `get_next_task` then hands it out again, and the old `cancellation_reason` is still sitting there since nothing clears it. This matches the reported symptom exactly.

## Fix

Added the same `cancelled` guard `claimTask` already has, in `releaseTask`:

```ts
if (task.status === "done" || task.status === "cancelled") {
  throw new Error(`Task ${taskId} is already ${task.status}, nothing to release`);
}
```
